questions.prompt: If a file has two lines and each readLine reads one line, how many calls read the whole file?
questions.answer: Two calls, assuming both lines are read and no additional data.
options: Two calls, assuming both lines are read OR no additional data.
Two calls, assuming both lines are not read and no additional data.
Two calls, assuming both lines are read and no additional data.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Two calls, assuming both lines are read and no additional data.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: openRead — Open a file for reading using OCR A Level pseudocode.
readLine — Read the next line from an open file.
endOfFile — Test whether no unread lines remain.
openWrite — Open for writing; existing file contents are replaced.
close — Release an opened file resource.

blocks.title: Open the resource
blocks.text: openRead returns a file object for reading; it does not overwrite the file.

blocks.title: Read until EOF
blocks.text: endOfFile() is false while another line remains. readLine() retrieves one line and moves the file position.

blocks.title: Close the file
blocks.text: After the final line, endOfFile() is true, so the loop stops and the file is closed. For writing use openWrite, writeLine, then close(); unlike reading, opening for writing overwrites any existing file contents.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: The first call returns Apple and advances the file position.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model and check
blocks.text: The next call returns Pear; variable a stays Apple.
